summary: Sentinel is a three-layer early-warning system designed to monitor astronaut health during long-duration space missions. Developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, it integrates molecular biomarkers, physiological vitals, and behavioural indicators to predict health deterioration up to 72 hours in advance. Using a transparent logistic regression model, Sentinel identifies deviations from individual baselines, generates explainable risk alerts, and produces automated Flight Surgeon Logs. Designed to operate offline during communication blackouts, the prototype achieved an AUROC of 0.90 in simulations involving 150 astronauts. It explores whether molecular changes can provide earlier warnings than conventional health monitoring systems.
details: Sentinel is an AI-assisted astronaut health-monitoring system developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It combines three layers of health indicators: molecular biomarkers (IL-6, IL-10, MCP-1, etc.), physiological vitals (heart rate, SpO2, sleep), and behavioural patterns (communication frequency, journal sentiment, reaction time). Using personalised baselines and logistic regression, it predicts health deterioration within 72 hours, generates explainable risk alerts, and produces automated Flight Surgeon Logs. The project aims to enable proactive healthcare during deep-space missions, particularly where communication delays prevent immediate medical assistance. It was developed using Python, Scikit-learn, Pandas, NumPy, Matplotlib, and Streamlit, with NASA OSDR research informing biomarker selection. Its key innovation is combining biological, physiological, and behavioural data into an explainable, lightweight system capable of offline operation. The prototype achieved an AUROC of 0.90 on a simulated cohort of 150 astronauts. Key considerations included individual health baselines, false alarms, communication blackouts, computational efficiency, and prediction reliability. Note: Results are simulation-based; the system is a research prototype, not a certified medical device.
